title: The letters of the mind
hook: a lesson that starts on the board and ends up inside: in the Patti, each school letter becomes a lesson for the soul

segments.voice: Yesterday, sasai, the Patti's first letter: the One who fashioned the world is Master of all. Your line was he made it. Which ordinary thing looked made to you? A new week starts. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-six.

Some school lessons never stay at school. A teacher draws a number line on the board, and years later someone waiting on test results is counting the days along it in their head. A coach says keep your eyes on the ball, and it turns into advice about a marriage. The lesson leaves the classroom and moves inside. The Patti does that on purpose, letter after letter. And it says who the real student is. Today: the letters of the mind.
screen: `A LESSON THAT LEAVES THE CLASSROOM.` → `IT MOVES INSIDE.` → `WHO IS THE REAL STUDENT?`

segments.voice: Start with the Patti's center line, its Rahao. It speaks to one pupil, and the pupil is the mind. In paraphrase: why do you forget, foolish mind? So the slate isn't really on a desk. It's inside. Now watch three letters turn a school lesson into a lesson for the soul. Kakai, the letter K. In paraphrase: when the hair turns white, bright without any soap, the messengers of death arrive, and bind you in the chains of Maya. Kakai could have been a line about anything. Guru Nanak makes it about gray hair in the mirror, and what it's quietly teaching. Dadai, the letter D. In paraphrase: I blame no one else; the blame lies in my own deeds. Whatever I did, that I received. Don't blame other people. On a school board, D is a shape to copy. In the mind, it's the hardest lesson there is: to stop pointing outward first. Tatai, a hard T. In paraphrase: why put on a show, mortal? In a moment, any moment, you may have to get up and go. Don't gamble your life away; run to the Lord's shelter. A schoolchild learns that letter by tracing it. The mind learns it by remembering it is not staying forever. Here's what ties them together. A school lesson is about the letter. A soul's lesson is about the one learning it. The Patti keeps both. You still learn your letters. But each one comes with a question for whoever is holding the pen. Today's line: the soul's lessons.
screen: `THE STUDENT IS THE MIND.` · `KAKAI: WHITE HAIR TEACHES.` · `DADAI: BLAME NO ONE ELSE.` · `TATAI: YOU WON'T STAY FOREVER.` · then, large: `THE SOUL'S LESSONS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: turn one lesson inward. Settle, and breathe. Think of something you learned as a child, a rule, a skill, a saying: share, look both ways, measure twice. Hold it for a moment as it was first taught. Then ask it the Patti's kind of question: what is this teaching the mind, not just the hands? Look both ways might become: pause before I speak. Let one answer come, and don't push for a clever one. If you pray, you can say Waheguru on the out-breath. The bell holds the time.
The letters of the mind. In the Patti, each letter turns a school lesson into a lesson for the soul, and the student the Rahao speaks to is the mind. Today's word.
screen: `THE LETTERS OF THE MIND — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: the soul's lessons. Today, when something goes wrong, try the letter dadai first: look at your own part before anyone else's. Day one thousand one hundred fifty-six.

howItsDone: In kirtan and katha the Patti is sung and explained stanza by stanza, and teachers draw out the inner lesson each letter carries, so a Gurmukhi letter becomes a reminder about the mind.
